'''''Beaucarnea recurvata''''', the '''elephant's foot'''<ref name=RHS/> or '''ponytail palm''',<ref name=EOL>{{EOL}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Asparagaceae]].<ref name=POWO>{{cite web |url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:531735-1 |title= Beaucarnea recurvata (K.Koch & Fintelm.) Lem. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=April 28, 2025}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url= https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/L5J8 |title= Beaucarnea recurvata (K.Koch & Fintelm.) Lem. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=April 28, 2025}}</ref> The species is [[endemism|endemic]] to eastern [[Mexico]]; according to [[IUCN]] it is now confined to the state of [[Veracruz]],<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" /> but [[Plants of the World Online]] also cites it as occurring in [[Oaxaca]], [[Puebla]], [[San Luis Potosí]], and [[Tamaulipas]].<ref name=POWO/><ref>{{cite book |title=Agaves, Yuccas, and Related Plants: A Gardener's Guide |first=Gary |last=Irish |publisher=Timber Press |year=2000 |isbn=978-0-88192-442-8 |page=[https://archive.org/details/agavesyuccasrela0000iris/page/187 187] |url=https://archive.org/details/agavesyuccasrela0000iris|url-access=registration }}</ref> Despite its common name, it is not closely related to the true palms ([[Arecaceae]]). It has become popular in Europe and worldwide as an [[ornamental plant]]. There are 350-year-old Beaucarneas registered in Mexico.<ref>Instituto de Ecología A.C. video files, Mexico</ref>

==Description==
It is an [[evergreen]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] growing to {{convert|8|m}} in height, with an enormously expanded [[caudex]] for storing water.<ref name="RHSD">{{cite book | last=Huxley | first=Anthony | last2=Griffiths | first2=Mark | last3=Levy | first3=Margot | title=The New Royal horticultural society dictionary of gardening | publisher=Macmillan Stockton press | publication-place=London New York | date=1992 | isbn=1-56159-001-0 | volume=3 | page=324}}</ref> This caudex can be as great as {{cvt|14|m}} girth in the wild.<ref>The Beaucarnea- Calabanus Clad https://www.explorelifeoearth.org/beaucarnea.html </ref><ref> Dave's Garden https://.com/guides/articles/view/261/ </ref> The single palm-like stem produces terminal tufts of strap-shaped, recurved leathery leaves, sometimes hair lock-shaped in the ends, and with occasional [[panicle]]s of small white flowers once the plant reaches over 10 years of age.

The [[Trunk (botany)|trunk]] is swollen at the base and slender higher up; young plants are unbranched, but become well branched with age. The almost spherical [[caudex]] in the youth stage later becomes broadly conic and very wide at the base. The [[bark (botany)|bark]] is smooth or finely cracked. The leaves are green, linear, slightly recurved and bent, thin, flat or slightly ridged. They are up to {{cvt|180|cm}} long and up to {{cvt|2|cm}} wide.<ref name="RHSD"/> The [[flower]]s are creamy-white, 1.5 mm diameter, produced in a dense panicle {{cvt|90–112|cm}} tall.<ref name="RHSD"/>

==Habitat==
''Beaucarnea recurvata'' occurs over an altitudinal range of {{cvt|200 to 900|m}} above sea level.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021"/> It grows on rocky soils deficient in nutrients, cliffs and steep mountains, where it grows in full sun or partial shade. Its habitat is low deciduous forest, with average temperatures of {{cvt|20|C}} and an annual rainfall of {{cvt|800|mm}}, and a well-marked dry season of between 7 and 8 months. The plants are very slow growing and very tolerant to drought.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Miranda |first1=Faustino |last2=Hernández-X |first2=Efraim |date=1963 |title=The types of vegetation of Mexico and their classification |journal=Boletín de la Sociedad Botánica de México |volume=28 |pages=29–72 |doi=10.17129/botsci.1084|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Conservation ==
The species of the genus ''[[Beaucarnea]]'' are mostly in critical condition due to various anthropogenic activities, which has led to severe fragmentation and destruction of their habitat. Additionally, the collection of seeds, seedlings, juveniles and adults for commercial use has affected population size and the proportion of sexes, thereby reducing fertilization possibilities and, consequently, seed production.<ref>Hernández SL, M. Martínez, G. Malda B., HA Castillo G., O. Salcedo G., Osorio R. Ma. L., A. Contreras H., R. Orellana L., C. Swords M., LE Carrillo S., KKE Almanza R., M. Capdevielle V, Ml Á. Herrera A. and M. Á. Pérez F. 2010. Final project report (ORN_PTA 09). Collection of elephant foot accessions (''Beaucarnea'' spp.) for germplasm conservation in Mexico . Autonomous University of Queretaro. 54 p.</ref> This exploitation process exposes this species, in a state of threat or extinction, by reducing the minimum viable size of the populations, as well as the deterioration of their genetic diversity.<ref name=":0" /> ''Beaucarnea recurvata'', is considered to be threatened according to Official Mexican Standard 059-ECOL-2010 of [[SEMARNAT]] in Mexico.

The species is listed in Appendix II of the [[Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species]] (CITES) meaning international trade in the species and its parts/derivatives is regulated by the CITES permitting system.<ref name="CITES"/>

==Cultivation== 
Having gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]],<ref name=RHS>{{cite web |title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Beaucarnea recurvata'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/1993/Beaucarnea-recurvata/Details |access-date=15 April 2020}}</ref> ''B. recurvata'' is often grown as a [[houseplant]], or an outdoor plant in [[temperateness|subtropical]] climate gardens. Slow-growing and drought-tolerant, ''Beaucarnea recurvata'' is [[hardiness (plants)|hardy]] to {{convert|10|°C|°F}}, grows in full sun to light shade, and requires proper soil mix to drain when watered. Overwatering  fosters pests such as the [[mealybug]] and [[cochineal]] insects. If kept in regions with winter frost, it must be an indoor plant as it cannot withstand cold temperatures. To maintain its original shape, the ends of its leaves should not be snipped, and when repotted it must keep all of its roots.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Nason |first1=John D. |last2=Hamrick |first2=J. L. |date=1997 |title=Reproductive and Genetic Consequences of Forest Fragmentation: Two Case Studies of Neotropical Canopy Trees |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/255658715 |journal=[[Journal of Heredity]] |volume=88 |issue=4 |pages=264–276 |doi=10.1093/oxfordjournals.jhered.a023104 |via=[[ResearchGate]]|doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Toxicity==
The species is not toxic to dogs, cats or horses.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bottle Palm |url=https://www.aspca.org/pet-care/animal-poison-control/toxic-and-non-toxic-plants/bottle-palm |website=ASPCA |access-date=5 August 2023 |language=en}}</ref>
